operations.summary: Mark a callback done or not a lead, or reopen a closed one, recorded against a named person (their people slug) and the time. `do` is the verb. An API-key call must name the person with exactly one of `actor` (people slug) or `as_user_id` (WordPress user id); a signed-in SyteOps Admin who names nobody acts as themselves. A slug is accepted only while it belongs to the current holder of its Users slot (422 actor_not_current). 422 actor_unresolved answers an unknown actor slug, an as_user_id with no people-registry entry, and a signed-in SyteOps Admin with no registry entry who names nobody; sending both actor and as_user_id is 422 actor_required. 403 actor_not_permitted when the Callbacks access of that person does not allow acting. A second request on an already-handled callback, or reopen on a callback that is not closed, changes nothing and says who acted and when (changed:false, already:true). Refused 422 invalid_action for any other `do`, 404 not_found for an unknown id, 409 state_changed when the callback moved under two attempts, 409 contact_details_not_full while contact details are not stored in Full, 409 callbacks_disabled when the RingTonic integration is off, 409 module_unavailable while Lead Attribution is off, and 409 in_flight while the same request is still being applied.

do.description: done, not_lead or reopen (reopen applies only to a done, not_lead or expired callback).

actor.description: People slug of the person acting; must be a current slot holder.

as_user_id.description: WordPress user id of the person acting, resolved to their people slug. Use instead of actor.

operations.summary: Read the Leads settings as the code uses them (the effective value `wp syteops leads setting get` prints), with each key's type, whether it may be written, and whether it is masked. A webhook address (masked) reads '' when empty and '[set]' otherwise; it is never returned. pii_mode is the mode in force, through the syteops_leads_pii_mode filter the contact-details writers apply. `notes` names a key stored in an older shape, or the stored pii_mode when a filter overrides it. Never returns a RingTonic secret (they are not settings).

keys.description: Only these setting keys (default: all). An entry that is not a string is 422 invalid_params; an unknown key is 422 unknown_setting.

operations.returns: data: {settings: {key: value}, keys: {key: {type, writable, masked, egress, confirm}}, notes: {key: note}}. egress: the key decides where lead data is sent. confirm: changing it on leads.settings_set needs confirm: true (pii_mode, ringtonic_store_call_summary and every egress key; ringtonic_contact_internal only when set to push).

operations.summary: Set one or more Leads settings in one write, all or nothing, with the settings screen's own rule for each key (the same table `wp syteops leads setting set` uses): a value the screen would quietly correct is refused. Keys are applied in the screen's order, so consent_mode lands before consent_cookie. Refused with 422 and nothing written: an unknown key (unknown_setting), ringtonic_noabort (screen_only_setting: it edits .htaccess), a RingTonic secret by any name (secret_setting: secrets are never written through this API; set them from a terminal with `wp syteops systems-api set --stdin`), a value the rules refuse (invalid_setting). A change to pii_mode (how contact details are stored) or to a key that decides where lead contact details are sent (crm_webhook_url, automation_webhook_url, recipient_emails, email_reply_to, callbacks_summary_slots, callbacks_reminder_slots, callbacks_weekly_slots, callbacks_reminders_enabled, callbacks_deal_summary_enabled), or turns on a switch that sends lead details off-site (automation_webhook_enabled, crm_webhook_enabled, email_instant_enabled, email_periodic_enabled, ringtonic_contact_forms, ringtonic_contact_field_names, ringtonic_contact_internal=push), or changes ringtonic_store_call_summary, needs confirm:true (409 confirmation_required, naming the keys); resending the current value does not. The confirm is one explicit step for every caller, not a role check. changed is false and nothing is written when no stored value would change.

settings.description: A non-empty object of {setting: value}; see settings_get for the keys and types. Lists and maps are JSON values.

confirm.description: true to change pii_mode, ringtonic_store_call_summary, a lead-data destination (the two webhook addresses, recipient_emails, email_reply_to, callbacks_summary_slots, callbacks_reminder_slots, callbacks_weekly_slots, callbacks_reminders_enabled, callbacks_deal_summary_enabled) or an off-site switch (automation_webhook_enabled, crm_webhook_enabled, email_instant_enabled, email_periodic_enabled, ringtonic_contact_forms, ringtonic_contact_field_names, ringtonic_contact_internal=push).

The path never changes. 404 not_found, 422 alias_not_editable (an alias follows its main link: edit the main link), 422 invalid_destination.

operations.summary: Permanently delete a main tracked link and every alias of it, freeing their paths. Destructive: needs confirm:true (409 confirmation_required without it) and a success leaves the lasting manage_destructive record. To see what a delete would remove first, read the link with tracked_link_list (with_clicks true): its aliases and all-time clicks. 404 not_found; 422 alias_not_editable (an alias is removed with its main link: delete that). The link's click events are NOT deleted: they stay in the events table and stop matching any link, so `clicks_orphaned` counts the events left unattributed and `clicks_removed` is always 0.
operations.returns: data: {deleted (the link id), aliases_deleted, clicks_removed (always 0: no click rows are deleted), clicks_orphaned (the link's lifetime click events, left in place but no longer attributed to any link)}

operations.summary: Give an ownerless main link a new path, keeping its id so its click history stays attached. A new_path that is already an alias OF THIS LINK is swapped in as the main path. All or nothing (one transaction): a failure leaves the old path serving and writes 500 write_failed. 404 not_found; 409 path_collision (another link, a page or post, or an archive); 422 invalid_path (not usable, reserved, or the link's current path), alias_not_editable (an alias id), rename_not_allowed (a link that has an owner: its path follows its link-set template and the Move tool).

keep_old_as_alias.description: true (default) keeps the old path answering as an alias of the link; false frees it.

operations.returns: data: {link: {id, path, destination, kind, owner_slug, active, aliases[], tags{}, fragment, person_anchor}}

operations.summary: LEGACY (deprecated: use delete_preview then delete_confirmed). Permanently delete one lead and everything this plugin keeps for it (the same purge as delete_confirmed), with no preview and no token. Its RingTonic step is unchanged: a fire-and-forget request to move the contact to "lost" (never a delete), reported as `ringtonic`: lost_requested (sent, not confirmed), no_contact, not_configured or not_sent. Checks no blocker and takes no lock. A refused or failed delete is 500 delete_failed (data left in place) or delete_partial (part of it removed), with data {id, deleted: false, ringtonic, removed}.

Read-only. Show exactly what a permanent delete of up to 25 leads would remove, with no names, emails, phones or messages: per lead a short label (status, created date, source), the counts of every kind of stored data, the RingTonic contact and what each RingTonic choice would do, and any blockers. When nothing blocks, it returns a confirm_token (valid 10 minutes, bound to these ids, these counts and the caller) for delete_confirmed. Send exactly one of id or ids; an id that is not a lead is the blocker not_found. The ids are read as one batch deleted in ascending order: a callback row or session click rows held only by leads of the batch are removed with the last of them (callbacks_with_batch / click_rows_with_batch at the earlier ones), never counted as shared.

ids.description: A JSON list of 1 to 25 lead ids (positive whole numbers). Send this or id, not both.

operations.returns: data: {ids[] (sorted), leads[]: {id, found, label{status, created, source (paid, organic, social, email, referral, direct or unknown)}, counts{events, click_rows, click_rows_shared, click_rows_with_batch, callbacks, callbacks_shared, callbacks_with_batch, callback_events, calls, transcripts, shared_events_unlinked, shared_names_cleared, attachments, meta, options, cron, pending_outbox}, ringtonic{linked, uuid_known, on_soft_delete, on_leave}, blockers[]}, deletable, confirm_token (null unless deletable), expires_at (null unless deletable)}

operations.summary: Destructive. Permanently delete the leads a delete_preview showed, and everything this plugin keeps for them. Needs confirm:true, the preview's confirm_token and the same ids; the preview is recomputed and any difference refuses the whole call with nothing deleted: 409 token_invalid (malformed or not this preview: another id set, other counts, another caller), 409 token_expired, 409 blocked (data.leads names the blockers), 404 not_found (an id that is no longer a lead, so a repeat after success is a clean not_found). `ringtonic` is required when any lead has a RingTonic contact (422 ringtonic_choice_required): soft_delete sends DELETE /contacts/{uuid} first (a 404 counts as already gone; any other failure stops the call there, 502 ringtonic_failed, with that lead untouched), leave keeps the contact and says so. RingTonic's delete is soft: it keeps a recoverable copy that a later contact push restores. soft_delete is refused 409 ringtonic_uuid_unknown for a lead whose contact uuid is not known and 409 ringtonic_unavailable while RingTonic is off. Each lead is then locked and checked again right before its own RingTonic step: 409 delete_in_progress (another call holds it) or 409 lead_changed (a change or a new blocker since the check) stops there, the leads after it not_attempted. A lead whose local delete could not run now (purge hooks detached, a pre_delete_post veto) is refused 500 delete_failed BEFORE any RingTonic request. A refused or failed local delete is 500 delete_failed (the lead untouched) or 500 delete_partial (part of its data removed); a hook that throws stops the call there with the results so far (hook_error warning). One lasting audit row per deleted lead; audit_recorded is false, with a warnings entry, when one could not be written.

ids.description: The same JSON list of 1 to 25 lead ids the preview was made for.

ringtonic.description: soft_delete or leave. Required when any of the leads has a RingTonic contact.

operations.returns: data: {deleted[] (lead ids), results[]: {id, status (deleted, failed, partial or not_attempted), removed{} (the preview's count keys), ringtonic{choice, outcome (no_contact, kept, deleted, already_gone, failed, transport or not_attempted), http}}, audit_recorded, warnings[]: {code: audit_not_recorded|hook_error, id}, ringtonic_note}

Returns 404 post_not_found for a missing, trashed or non-viewable post (and post_id 0), and 403 forbidden for a signed-in caller without edit_post on it; an API key skips only the edit_post check.
List pipeline run-history ledger rows (paginated; filter by post/recipe/status).
Get one run-history row by id (includes decoded per-stage results).
Delete ONE run-history row (confirm:true). Leaves a lasting run_deleted record. 404 not_found when the row is gone; 409 deletion_record_protected for a deletion-record row, which is never removed.
Clear ALL run history and mirrored activity (confirm:true). The lasting deletion records are kept, and a runs_cleared record with the count is written.
Run-history counters shown on the pipelines dashboard.

The Log view activity feed, newest first. per_page 1-100 (default 25), page 1-10000; out-of-range values return 422. Rows carry only id, created_at, event, status, actor, post and an allowlisted meta; never a review link or token.
List all configured pipeline recipes.
Get one recipe by id.
Create a pipeline recipe. Refuses with 409 recipe_exists when a recipe with that id (default: the slug of name) already exists; use update_recipe to change an existing one.
Update an existing pipeline recipe (merge-patch: omitted top-level keys are preserved, but a supplied trigger or policy replaces that whole sub-object — send the full sub-object to change one field).
Delete a pipeline recipe (the default recipe cannot be deleted).

Read the Content Pipelines operating mode: setup or production. The Review Portal stays fully usable: setup mode does NOT stop review.approve or calendar publishing.

Switch the Content Pipelines mode. Production lets ingested posts take their source's configured status and turns on run history, the workflow forward, social sends and the pipeline emails. Setup still ingests and builds posts, but forces newly ingested posts to draft, writes no run-history rows, skips the workflow forward and the new-post reviewer email, holds social sends until production, and skips the 'Now live', schedule-change and held-source alert emails. operations.summary: Turn GEO generation on or off, the same switch as the provider card. Turning it off while LLMS Amplifier is the GEO engine is 409 amplifier_owns_geo.
Turn LLMS Amplifier on or off as the GEO engine. Enabling returns 409 plugin_not_installed when the Amplifier plugin is absent.
List all configured content sources (never includes the secret).
operations.returns: data.sources[]: array of {id, name, slug, enabled, status, auth_mode, target_post_type, cpt_post_type, shape_fingerprint, mapping, mapping_status, sample, default_author_id, pin_author, default_reviewers, default_ccs, default_post_status, meta_fields, fm_variables, forward_enabled, forward_url, forward_auth_mode, created_at, updated_at} (secret and forward_secret are never included)

Export one content source as a portable setup package (no secrets, no posts).
operations.returns: data: envelope {format, schema_version, payload, ...} — never includes secret or forward_secret

operations.returns: data: {id, name, slug, mode, secret, secret_source, ...} — secret is plaintext and NON-EMPTY only when secret_source is "generated"

operations.summary: Replay a source's last captured payload through the ingest core. Destructive: it creates or updates the article with the source's own settings, so a source set to publish publishes it, a source in overwrite mode overwrites reviewer edits on an article already live, and the draft core spends an AI call. Shares the source's daily AI allowance (default 10 a day, UTC) with learn_from_sample.
operations.returns: data: {outcome, message, post_id, created, edit_link}; changed is false for a held or protected article. 404 not_found (unknown or disabled source), 409 confirmation_required or no_payload, 422 invalid_json, 429 learn_cap_reached

operations.summary: Ask the Ingest AI area to propose a field mapping from the source's captured sample. The proposal REPLACES the stored mapping and is never approved: on a source whose mapping was approved, new deliveries are held until it is approved again, so that call needs confirm:true. Spends an AI call and shares the source's daily AI allowance (default 10 a day, UTC) with reprocess.

confirm.description: Required (true) when the source's mapping is approved.

operations.returns: data: {mapping}; changed is true. 404 not_found, 409 confirmation_required, no_provider or no_sample, 422 invalid_sample, 429 learn_cap_reached, 502 ai_empty_response or invalid_json, 503 ai_unavailable

operations.summary: Preview a mapping against a sample payload without writing anything.

sample.description: The sample payload, as a JSON object.

mapping.description: Optional field => {path, transform} rows to try; omit to test the source's stored mapping.

operations.returns: data: {normalized, empty_fields}. 404 not_found, 422 no_sample (an empty sample object)

operations.summary: Re-send the review email for a post to its own reviewers (never to a caller-supplied address); one resend per post every 2 minutes.
operations.returns: data: {message, notify:{outcome, partial, summary}} (display names only, no addresses or links). 404 post_not_found, 409 module_unavailable, 429 resend_cooldown, 400 no_recipients, 500 send_failed

operations.summary: Get the per-site business identity (company facts) map.
Update business identity fields (partial map; unknown keys rejected).

Read the Squirrly IndexNow state: whether SyteOps may send, why not, the queue, the last result and, with post_id, that post's eligibility. With post_id, a missing, trashed or non-viewable post is 404 post_not_found and a signed-in caller who cannot edit it is 403 forbidden.
operations.returns: data: {state, reason, enabled, squirrly_version, auto_indexing, post_types[], key_stored, paused, queue: {count, next_run}, last: {time, post_id, kind, result, http}, post?: {post_id, eligible, reason, last}}

operations.summary: Queue one live post for IndexNow. It is not sent inside this request: it goes out through the normal queue about a minute later, and Squirrly's 24-hour rule still applies. A missing, trashed or non-viewable post is 404 post_not_found and a signed-in caller who cannot edit it is 403 forbidden.
Recompute the agent-prompt guard hash (CANON-1) for one Elementor element so a session can compare it before writing. Returns the hash and its key list only, never a setting value.
Read one post's SEO title, description and focus keywords from whichever SEO tool is active. With no active SEO tool it returns 409 no_active_seo_tool.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, tool, tool_label, fields: {title, description, keywords}}

operations.summary: Write one post's SEO title, description or focus keywords through the active SEO tool's own writer. Use this, not update_content meta, for every SEO plugin. dry_run:true writes nothing and returns each field's current and proposed value; a real write returns 409 confirmation_required until confirm:true. Only the fields sent change; any other field is refused. Caps: title 300, description 1000, keywords 500 characters. A placeholder the SEO tool fills from site data is refused (422 seo_token_not_allowed) unless allow_placeholders:true.

title.description: SEO title. Send an empty string to clear it.

description.description: Meta description. Send an empty string to clear it.

keywords.description: Focus keywords, comma-separated. Send an empty string to clear it.

allow_placeholders.description: JSON true only. Allow placeholders the SEO tool fills from site data (custom fields, options). Off by default; only safe ones such as the post title are accepted without it.

operations.returns: data: {post_id, tool, tool_label, dry_run, changed, written, fields: {<field>: {current, proposed, changed}}, placeholders: {<field>: []}, stored?: {title, description, keywords}, note?}

operations.summary: Purge one post's page (post_id), or up to 30 URLs on this site's own host (urls), from LiteSpeed and Cloudflare when present. With post_id it also purges the pages that show the post (home, blog index, category and tag archives, author page, main feed, post type archive, SEO sitemaps) when the related-pages setting allows it (Off is the post's own page alone), and, when that post is built with Elementor, clears and rebuilds that post's generated CSS before the purge (elementor_css_scope post), or clears the Elementor CSS site-wide (elementor_css_scope site_wide) for the Kit, header, footer and other site-wide templates, when the Regenerate Elementor CSS setting is off, or when the per-post rebuild cannot run; a site-wide clear is answered by a background rebuild of every page's CSS and one site purge. layers reports each cache layer: litespeed is attempted (it cannot confirm), partial, error or skipped; cloudflare is purged, partial, error, skipped or off (the Cloudflare purge mode setting; off is also listed in skipped, and zone mode purges the whole zone even for one URL). queued is true and deferred is zone when, in the zone purge mode, the minimum interval since the last full purge held the Cloudflare zone purge back: the pages are purged in LiteSpeed now and the zone purge is booked for when the interval ends. not_run with reentrant in skipped means a purge was already running and nothing was done. Send post_id or urls, not both; a URL on any other host refuses the whole call.

urls.description: List of absolute http(s) URLs on this site's host, at most 30.

operations.returns: data: {urls[], purged[], attempted[], skipped[], errors[], layers: {litespeed: {status}, cloudflare: {status, mode, reason?}}, queued, deferred?, elementor_css: regenerated|cleared|unavailable|not_elementor|null, elementor_css_scope: post|site_wide|null}

operations.summary: Read-only. How the page cache stands on this site, from one function the Page cache card also uses: which layers are present (LiteSpeed Cache with its public, front page and feed lifetimes in seconds and whether the public lifetime is longer than the warning limit, Cloudflare with its purge mode, Elementor), each layer's last purge outcome, whether WP-Cron is disabled, and a trace of the carry endpoint that delivers LiteSpeed's purge. The trace is bounded: the time of the last recorded answer, of the last answer to a nudge and to a visitor, counts of RECORDED answers (not requests; an answer that found nothing waiting is recorded at most once every 30 seconds), up to 20 recent answers newest first, and waiting, a COUNT of purges no response has carried yet. A source of nudge means a nudge arrived at the carry endpoint, which is unauthenticated: anyone can send one, so it is evidence that something called, never proof that the cron Worker did; cross-check the origin access log. A time is a Unix second or null; a lifetime of 0 means not cached and null means unknown. No page URL, token, zone id or error text is returned. A plugin older than this operation answers 404 unknown_operation.
operations.returns: data: {layers: {litespeed: {present, lifetime: {public, frontpage, feed, warn_after, long}|null, last: {at, status, scope, reason, urls, errors, delivery?, why?}|null}, cloudflare: {present, mode: urls|zone|off, last}, elementor: {present}}, cron: {wp_cron_disabled}, carry: {last_served_at, last_nudge_at, last_visitor_at, counts: {nudge, visitor, carried}, recent: [{at, source: nudge|visitor, carried}], waiting}}

operations.summary: One page of a person's Review Portal queue, as that person sees it. list is pending (default), watching, live, live_posts, live_pages, coming_up or notes. An API-key call must send as_user_id (the person whose queue to read; 422 as_user_id_required otherwise, 404 user_not_found when no such user); a signed-in SyteOps Admin defaults to themselves. per_page is 5, 10, 25 or 100. Page with the returned next_cursor. No review links are returned.

list.description: pending (default), watching, live, live_posts, live_pages, coming_up or notes.

operations.returns: data: {as_user_id, list, rows[], has_more, next_cursor, truncated, page_count}; a post row is {post_id, title, source, received, scheduled_ts, modified_ts, feedback_count, changes_requested, qa}, a notes row is {post_id, title, author, excerpt, created, note_id}

operations.summary: One post's review status: post status, whether changes are requested, open and total note counts, the reviewers and watchers, and the latest recorded activity. A missing, trashed or non-viewable post is 404 post_not_found.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, title, post_status, changes_requested, open_notes, total_notes, reviewers[], watchers[], last_activity: {event, at}|null}; a person is {user_id, display_name, roles[]}

operations.summary: The people who may review one post and the people watching it. Ids, display names and roles only; no email addresses.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, reviewers[], watchers[]}; a person is {user_id, display_name, roles[]}

operations.summary: One post's review notes and replies, oldest first, as the portal shows them. per_page is 1 to 100 (default 25). A note made in one device size can carry a comment per other size: they are listed in views as {px, text}, never as notes of their own, and never counted in total. A comment sent with the note that has not yet become a measured size is listed with queued: true.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, total, page, per_page, has_more, comments[]}; a comment is {id, parent, user_id, user_name, note, created_at, kind, target_kind, att_id, resolved, via_api, views, bp_px?, breakpoint?, breakpoint_label?}; via_api is true for a note written through this API; bp_px (integer, 320 to 2560) is the exact preview width a picture or element note was made at, breakpoint its stored key (desktop, laptop, tablet_landscape, tablet, mobile or custom, where custom is a typed width) and breakpoint_label the display name the agent prompt uses (for example Custom width); each is present only when the note stored it, and a reply or an article-level note has none; views is always present: [{px, text, queued?}] widest first, one per other device size where the card holds its own comment (note is the comment for the size the card was made in), queued true while a comment waits for the author's width walk, [] when none or for a reply

operations.summary: Add a reviewer to one post, as the portal's Send to a colleague does: the person is emailed that they were asked to help review, the post's review link gets a fresh expiry window, and the post's activity log records it. Adding a reviewer lets that person open and edit the post, and publish it when who_can_publish is any. Under who_can_publish=author_approver they can edit but not publish, unless they are the post's author or a site administrator or SyteOps Admin. user_id must be a SyteOps user linked to a WordPress account (422 user_not_selectable; 404 user_not_found when no such account). A post that was never sent for review is refused (409 not_review_managed). A watcher who is added as a reviewer stops being a watcher. Someone already listed is ok with changed:false and is not emailed again.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, user_id, emailed, notify: {outcome: sent|queued|failed|off|none, partial}, reviewers[], watchers[]}; emailed and notify only when the person was added; a person is {user_id, display_name, roles[]}

operations.summary: Remove a reviewer from one post: they can no longer open, edit or publish it through the portal (unless they are a site administrator, or a watcher or a bundle reviewer of it, which keeps that narrower access), and their queued review emails for it are dropped when they no longer have any access. The post's author stays on the list (409 author_protected). The removal sticks: the post's source default reviewers and CCs do not put them back. Someone not listed is ok with changed:false. No email is sent; the activity log records it.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, user_id, reviewers[], watchers[]} (the lists after the call); a person is {user_id, display_name, roles[]}

operations.summary: Add a watcher to one post: they may open it and comment, and receive its routine review emails, but cannot edit or publish it. user_id must be a SyteOps user linked to a WordPress account (422 user_not_selectable). A post that was never sent for review is refused (409 not_review_managed). A reviewer of the post is refused (409 already_reviewer). Someone already watching is ok with changed:false. No email is sent; the activity log records it.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, user_id, reviewers[], watchers[]} (the lists after the call); a person is {user_id, display_name, roles[]}

operations.summary: Remove a watcher from one post: they can no longer open or comment on it unless something else grants that, and their queued review emails for it are then dropped. The removal sticks: the post's source default CCs do not put them back. Someone not watching is ok with changed:false. No email is sent; the activity log records it.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, user_id, reviewers[], watchers[]} (the lists after the call); a person is {user_id, display_name, roles[]}

operations.summary: Approve a post for publishing, as the Review Portal's Publish does with nothing edited: it publishes now, or schedules it when the post holds a reviewer's intended time or a reserved cadence slot at least a minute ahead and scheduling is on. A post already scheduled keeps its own date: with scheduling on and the date at least a minute ahead it is ok with changed:false and already_scheduled:true, and nothing is written, logged or emailed; with scheduling off that date could not be kept, so it is refused (409 scheduling_off; unschedule it first to publish now). A scheduled date already due (a missed schedule) publishes with that date. Acts with admin authority: an admin or API-key caller bypasses the post's reviewer list and the who_can_publish rule, which gate people in the portal, and is limited to posts in review. It records the approver as user 0 whenever the API key authorized the call, otherwise the signed-in SyteOps Admin. A post never sent for review (no reviewers and no review link) is refused (409 not_in_review). A post already live is ok with changed:false and already_live:true, and nothing is written, logged or emailed. A title, excerpt or body the call does not send is published exactly as stored. Every portal check applies: 409 not_ready (with failed[] requirements), 409 published_immutable, 500 publish_failed. Open notes do not block it (the portal only warns); open_notes reports them. Destructive: send confirm:true.

confirm.description: Must be true: this puts a post live.

operations.returns: data: {post_id, status, scheduled, scheduled_readable, permalink, emailed, notify: {outcome, partial}, images: {imported, reused, failed, capped}|null, open_notes, approved_by: {user_id, via, api_key}, already_live, already_scheduled}

operations.summary: Send a post back for changes as one person, as the Review Portal's Request Changes does: records message as their note, cancels a pending schedule when they may publish, and emails the author and co-reviewers. The note is marked as added via API, and the portal's history says so. An API-key call must send as_user_id; a signed-in SyteOps Admin defaults to themselves. That person must be able to edit the post in the portal (403 forbidden); 409 schedule_due when it is about to publish and they cannot cancel it.

message.description: The note, plain text, up to the portal's note length.

operations.returns: data: {post_id, as_user_id, entry: {id, parent, kind, created_at, via_api}, emailed, notify: {outcome, partial}, unscheduled, status}

operations.summary: Add a review note as one person, through the Review Portal's own writer, so the notes email batches it the same way. Send exactly one target: parent_id (a reply to a top-level note; notify and resolve apply), attachment_id or image_url (a note on a picture), or element (a note pinned to a page element, with the portal's element fields such as selector, text and heading). The portal has no untargeted note; use request_changes for an article-level note. The note is marked as added via API, and the portal's history says so. An API-key call must send as_user_id; that person must be able to comment on the post (403 forbidden), and resolve needs edit rights.

parent_id.description: Reply to this top-level note id.

notify.description: Reply only: email the thread (default true).

resolve.description: Reply only: also resolve the parent note.

image_url.description: The picture's URL, when it has no attachment id.

element.description: Element target: selector, sig, text, ox, oy, vw, media, src, name, breakpoint, bp_px, tag, el_id, classes, heading, html, builder_path, rect, url, bld.

view_notes.description: Element note only: a comment per other device size, as {"768": "text", "390": "text"} (viewport width in px to plain text). At most 7 entries; a width must be 1 to 10000 and the text non-empty, capped to the note length; anything else is dropped. The comments are HELD on the note and become its per-size comments only when the note's author walks the page widths in the Review Portal and reaches that width; nothing is written for a size until then. The response view_notes_queued is how many were held.

operations.returns: data: {post_id, as_user_id, kind: reply|image|element, entry: {id, parent, kind, created_at, via_api}}; a reply adds {resolve: changed|unchanged|missing|failed|null (null when not asked), notified, notify: {outcome, partial}}; an element note sent with view_notes adds {view_notes_queued}, the number of per-size comments held on the note

operations.summary: The Review Portal's Portal Permissions as the settings screen reads them: who_can_publish (any or author_approver) and the per-area matrix, with a default row (everyone else), role rows keyed by SyteOps role slug and person rows keyed by user number. An absent role or person cell inherits; an absent default cell is that area's default. Also lists every area with its allowed values and whether this site's screen shows it, and the role and person rows that may be set (a person is listed only when linked to a WordPress account, as on the screen). A SyteOps Admin is never restricted by the matrix, and site administrators can always publish. Works before the portal is in use.
operations.returns: data: {who_can_publish, permissions: {default: {area: value}, roles: {slug: {area: value}}, users: {user_num: {area: value}}}, areas[]: {key, label, values[], default, shown}, roles[]: {slug, name}, users[]: {user_num, name}}

operations.summary: Change who can review and publish in the Review Portal. Partial: only the cells sent change, every other cell and row is kept. In roles and users a cell of inherit (or null) clears it and a row of null clears the whole row; the default row takes real values only. Every section, role slug, user number (a person linked to a WordPress account, as the screen lists), area and value is checked against the settings screen's own lists, and an area the screen does not show on this site is refused (422 invalid_permissions; nothing is written). who_can_publish is any or author_approver (422 invalid_who_can_publish). Switching to author_approver when no user holds the administrator publish override is refused (409 no_publisher_left). Send at least one of the two (422 nothing_to_change). One set runs at a time; a concurrent one is refused (409 busy) rather than risk losing a cell, so retry it. Saved through the screen's own validator and recorded in the activity log. Requires confirm:true.

permissions.description: Partial matrix: {default?: {area: value}, roles?: {slug: {area: value|inherit|null}|null}, users?: {user_num: {area: value|inherit|null}|null}}.

who_can_publish.description: any (any selected reviewer) or author_approver (the post author or an administrator).

operations.returns: data: {who_can_publish, permissions: {default, roles, users} as stored after the change, changes[]: {row, area, from, to}} (null = unset)

operations.summary: The Review Portal's site-wide email options. show_photos is the site default for whether a review email card carries the article's featured photo (on unless switched off). A person's own choice (users.update email_photos) overrides it in either direction and a person with none follows it; people_showing and people_hiding count the active people who have made one. Emails only: the photo on the site and in the portal is unaffected.

Set the site default for article photos in review emails. false leaves the photo off the cards in every review email (digest, new draft, updated draft, reminders and the rest) sent to anyone who has not chosen for themselves; true puts it back. A person's own choice (users.update email_photos) is never changed by this and still wins. Takes effect on the next email built, including one already queued. Not destructive: no confirm needed, and calling it again reverses it. show_photos must be the JSON value true or false (422 otherwise).

show_photos.description: JSON true (show the featured photo on review email cards, the default) or false (leave it off).

operations.returns: data: {show_photos, people_showing, people_hiding} as stored after the change

operations.summary: The publishing calendar for a window: scheduled and published posts in it (grid_events) plus the undated draft and pending rail. from and to are ISO 8601 dates (YYYY-MM-DD: whole days) or date-times, in the site timezone unless they carry Z or an offset, and the window may span at most 92 days (422 range_too_large). scope is pipeline (default, posts the content pipeline produced) or all. post_types, when sent, must be a list of calendar post types. grid_truncated is true when the window held more posts than the grid returns (500): narrow the window. The rail is not date-bounded: page it with rail_cursor and rail_per (5, 10, 25 or 100). A site-local time that the clocks skip is 422 date_in_dst_gap.

from.description: Window start: YYYY-MM-DD (start of that day) or an ISO 8601 date-time.

to.description: Window end: YYYY-MM-DD (end of that day) or an ISO 8601 date-time. At most 92 days after from.

post_types.description: A JSON list of calendar post type names, e.g. ["post", "page"]; a keyed object is refused.

rail_cursor.description: rail_next_cursor from the previous page, unchanged; anything else is 422 invalid_cursor.

operations.returns: data: {from_gmt, to_gmt, scope, grid_events[], grid_truncated, rail_drafts[], rail_has_more, rail_next_cursor, rail_truncated}; an event is {id, title, type, type_label, status, date_gmt, date_site, reserved, pipeline_origin}

operations.summary: Move a post's publication to a future moment, exactly as dragging it on the calendar does: a draft or pending post becomes scheduled, a scheduled post moves, and the schedule notice goes to the people the portal tells. date must be at least five minutes ahead (422 date_not_future), and the post is never published instead; a live post cannot be given a later date (409 published_immutable). A bad date is 422 invalid_date.

date.description: ISO 8601 date-time, e.g. 2026-11-03T09:00:00 (site timezone) or 2026-11-03T09:00:00Z / +02:00 (that instant).

operations.returns: data: {post_id, status, scheduled, intent, date_gmt, date_site, notify}; notify is the schedule notice outcome

operations.summary: Cancel a scheduled post's publication and return it to a draft (409 not_scheduled when it is not scheduled). Reversible: the cancelled moment is returned as previous_gmt and reschedule puts it back.

Take a LIVE post down and return it to a draft (409 not_published when it is not live). The site's static front page and posts page are refused (409 protected_page). The publication date is kept; pending post-publish recipe runs and social sends are stood down. Destructive: send confirm:true.

The next free publishing moment on the site's cadence after a time (default now). enabled is false and the slot empty when cadence is off; truncated means the walk could not read the calendar completely. exclude_post_id keeps that post out of its own conflicts. scope is all (default) or pipeline.

after.description: ISO 8601 date-time to search after (default now).

operations.returns: data: {enabled, truncated, slot_gmt, slot_site}; the slot strings are empty when none

operations.summary: Would scheduling this post at this moment break the site's publishing rhythm, and where would it fit instead? Advisory: nothing is written or refused. scope is all (default) or pipeline.

date.description: ISO 8601 date-time, e.g. 2026-11-03T09:00:00 (site timezone) or 2026-11-03T09:00:00Z / +02:00 (that instant).

operations.returns: data: {post_id, date_gmt, enabled, collides, reasons[], conflicts[], suggestion_label, suggestion_local, truncated}

operations.summary: Hold the next free cadence moment on a draft or pending post, as an arriving article gets one (a post already holding one is moved). Only a draft or pending post can hold a slot (409 not_holdable), and only a post type the calendar handles (422 unsupported_type). Not reserving is an answer: reserved is false with a reason of slots_disabled, cadence_opt_out or not_reserved.

Queue one social send for one article to a configured destination. when is time (default; send at fire_at, a Unix time in seconds between one minute and five years ahead) or on_publish (send when the article first goes live; fire_at not allowed). text is the final post text, up to 3000 characters (counted as characters, not bytes). A signed-in caller also needs publish capability for the post type (403 forbidden), as in the screen; a key skips that check. Refuses 409 social_disabled while Social Publishing is off, 422 bad_destination for an unknown destination_id, and 404 post_not_found for a missing, trashed or non-viewable post.

text.description: The final post text, up to 3000 characters.

fire_at.label: a Unix time in seconds
fire_at.description: Unix time in seconds; required when when is time.

operations.returns: data: {post_id, job_id, when, fire_at, destination: {id, name}}

operations.summary: Cancel one scheduled social send on an article, by the job_id social.schedule returned. Works while Social Publishing is off, so a pending send can always be stopped. 404 post_not_found for a missing, trashed or non-viewable post (trashing a post already drops its scheduled sends); 404 job_not_found when no such job is pending.

Build the listing-card image for each image the article owns that lacks a current one (the same unforced path a page render takes; images already current are left alone). With the repair on this queues paid jobs. At most 25 images per call. 409 listing_image_disabled when the feature is off; 429 cooldown (10 minutes per article, shared with reprocess, released when nothing was built or queued); 429 daily_limit when the site-wide daily allowance of images (100 by default, counted per image across run and reprocess, refunded when nothing was built or queued) is used up; processed and queued count only images built or newly queued, and changed is true only then; 404 post_not_found for a missing, trashed or non-viewable post.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, processed, queued, failed, skipped, items[] is {attachment_id, built, queued, error?, repaired?, reason?, retrying?}}

operations.summary: Rebuild the listing-card image for each image the article owns, from scratch, even when one looks current: the failure memo is cleared and the repair is re-queued (paid). The live crop stays until the new one replaces it, so this is not destructive. At most 25 images per call; same refusals, 10-minute per-article cooldown and site-wide daily image allowance as run.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, processed, queued, failed, skipped, items[] is {attachment_id, built, queued, error?, repaired?, reason?, retrying?}}

operations.summary: List the AI-generated and AI-remixed pictures with a verdict each. It writes no post data and no records (it may refresh the in-use check's own caches). bucket is removable (nothing uses it), possibly (it might be in use), in_use, live_source (the source of a picture in use) or kept (a manual keep, a file another row shares, a hidden or pipeline file, the source of a picture that might be in use, or a check that could not finish). reasons are sentences and codes are the same reasons as machine values (unused, in_use, live_source, possibly, manual_keep, shared_file, hidden_file, pipeline_image, source_of_possibly, could_not_check); only could_not_check is worth a rescan. file is the uploads-relative name and url the plain media URL. limit is 1 to 200 (default 50) and offset is 0 or more, else 422; next_offset is null on the last page. 409 module_unavailable when Content Pipelines is off.
operations.returns: data: {items[], total, counts{removable, possibly, in_use, live_source, kept}, next_offset}; an item is {id, bucket, reasons[], codes[], file, url, date, source_id, bytes}

operations.summary: The dry run of cleanup: judge the pictures fresh, write no post data, no zip and no record (it may refresh the in-use check's own caches), and say what cleanup would do. The pictures are would_remove, the rest are skipped with the reason; removed and failed are always empty and backup is null. Read-only, so it needs no confirm. Run it first and compare with the cleanup answer, which judges again when it writes.

ids.description: A JSON list of picture (attachment) ids, each a positive whole number: at most 25 for cleanup and at most 200 for cleanup_preview. Omit it to cover the next page of up to 25 AI pictures. A list that is empty, is longer than the limit or holds anything else is 422.

offset.label: a whole number
offset.description: Without ids: how many AI pictures to step over before the page (default 0); use next_offset from the previous answer. Refused with ids.

backup.description: JSON true (default) or false: put the originals in a zip first. A real boolean only; "false" or 0 is 422, never read as off. The preview accepts and ignores it so the same parameters serve both calls.

operations.returns: data: {dry_run, removed[], would_remove[], skipped{id: reason}, failed{id: reason}, backup: {file, bytes, count, trim_failed}|null, held, more, next_offset}. skipped reasons are the scan bucket (in_use, possibly, live_source, kept) or not_a_candidate, already_held (another run took it first), time_limit (the run stopped before reaching it: without ids more is then true and next_offset starts the next page at the first picture it did not reach; with ids send those ids again), over_limit, backup_failed; failed reasons are remove_failed or not_removed. trim_failed is true when the zip could not be cut down to the removed pictures: it is kept and named anyway (it also holds the originals of pictures that stayed, and with a holding period of 0 it is the only copy of the removed ones). held is true when removed pictures go to the recoverable Removed pictures list. more and next_offset say whether more AI pictures follow this page (never with ids)

operations.summary: Remove unused AI pictures. Destructive: send confirm:true on every call (preview first with cleanup_preview). Only a picture that is removable at the moment of removal goes; everything else is skipped with its reason, and the check is never bypassed. Pictures go to the recoverable Removed pictures list for the holding period (or are deleted at once when it is 0), and with backup (default true) their originals are zipped first: the answer names the zip by file name only and the API never serves it. Without ids it covers one page of up to 25 AI pictures; repeat with next_offset while more is true. With ids, at most 25 per call (422 above that); the preview takes up to 200. Writes one activity row and one run-log row when something was removed, none otherwise. 409 module_unavailable when Content Pipelines is off.

ids.description: A JSON list of picture (attachment) ids, each a positive whole number: at most 25 for cleanup and at most 200 for cleanup_preview. Omit it to cover the next page of up to 25 AI pictures. A list that is empty, is longer than the limit or holds anything else is 422.

offset.label: a whole number
offset.description: Without ids: how many AI pictures to step over before the page (default 0); use next_offset from the previous answer. Refused with ids.

backup.description: JSON true (default) or false: put the originals in a zip first. A real boolean only; "false" or 0 is 422, never read as off. The preview accepts and ignores it so the same parameters serve both calls.

operations.returns: data: {dry_run, removed[], would_remove[], skipped{id: reason}, failed{id: reason}, backup: {file, bytes, count, trim_failed}|null, held, more, next_offset}. skipped reasons are the scan bucket (in_use, possibly, live_source, kept) or not_a_candidate, already_held (another run took it first), time_limit (the run stopped before reaching it: without ids more is then true and next_offset starts the next page at the first picture it did not reach; with ids send those ids again), over_limit, backup_failed; failed reasons are remove_failed or not_removed. trim_failed is true when the zip could not be cut down to the removed pictures: it is kept and named anyway (it also holds the originals of pictures that stayed, and with a holding period of 0 it is the only copy of the removed ones). held is true when removed pictures go to the recoverable Removed pictures list. more and next_offset say whether more AI pictures follow this page (never with ids)

operations.summary: Read one person's saved LinkedIn groups, the list their Share to LinkedIn dialog offers. Read-only. Works whether or not the dialog is offered to that person right now. 404 user_not_found when user_id is not a WordPress user.

user_id.description: WordPress user id of the person whose saved LinkedIn groups to use. 404 user_not_found when no such user. Digits only; the list read or written is that person's and nobody else's.

operations.returns: data: {user_id, groups[], count, max}; groups is the person's whole list after the call, in saved order, each {id, name, url}: id is LinkedIn's numeric group id as a string, name the saved name, url the page the group opens at (https://www.linkedin.com/groups/{id}/); count is the number saved and max the most one person may save (20)

operations.summary: Save one LinkedIn group to one person's list, as their hub card does, and answer the updated list. address is either the numeric group id (1234567) or the group's own page address (https://www.linkedin.com/groups/1234567/, on linkedin.com or www.linkedin.com, with or without the closing slash; a query string or fragment is dropped); only the numeric id is stored. Any other host, a look-alike host, another scheme, a slug address, an extra path, a port, a user name in the address or a value with spaces is 422 invalid_address. name is plain text of 1 to 80 characters with no angle brackets: blank is 422 name_required and anything else wrong is 422 name_invalid (it is refused, never cleaned): too long, an angle bracket, a control character, an invisible or direction-changing character (zero-width and bidi marks; the joiner inside an emoji sequence is fine), or no visible character at all. A control character anywhere in address (a tab, a carriage return, a newline, a NUL) is 422 invalid_address; only plain spaces around it are ignored. The same group twice is 409 duplicate_group; a 21st group is 409 list_full (a person keeps at most 20); an unknown person is 404 user_not_found; a save that did not stick is 500 write_failed. Writes for one person are serialized on the server (a lock per person, so two calls cannot erase each other's add): a call that cannot get it within about 5 seconds is 409 busy, retryable, and nothing is written. Works whether or not the Share to LinkedIn dialog is offered to that person, so groups can be staged before it is. Not destructive. Writes only that person's list and leaves a debug-log line (person and group id only).

user_id.description: WordPress user id of the person whose saved LinkedIn groups to use. 404 user_not_found when no such user. Digits only; the list read or written is that person's and nobody else's.

name.description: The group's name as the person will see it in the dialog: plain text, 1 to 80 characters, no angle brackets, control characters or invisible characters. A JSON string only.

address.description: The LinkedIn group: its numeric id (1234567) or its page address (https://www.linkedin.com/groups/1234567/). A JSON string only; a number, boolean or list is 422 invalid_params.

operations.returns: data: {user_id, groups[], count, max}; groups is the person's whole list after the call, in saved order, each {id, name, url}: id is LinkedIn's numeric group id as a string, name the saved name, url the page the group opens at (https://www.linkedin.com/groups/{id}/); count is the number saved and max the most one person may save (20)

operations.summary: Remove one saved LinkedIn group from one person's list and answer the updated list. Destructive: send confirm:true on every call, or the answer is 409 confirmation_required and nothing changes. id is the group's numeric id exactly as list returns it (an address is not accepted here): a value that is not a numeric group id is 422 invalid_group_id, and an id that is not in that person's list is 404 group_not_found with nothing changed. An unknown person is 404 user_not_found; a save that did not stick is 500 write_failed; a call that cannot get the person's write lock within about 5 seconds is 409 busy, retryable, and nothing changes. Leaves a lasting activity row in the Content Pipelines ledger (a manage_destructive row with the person's user id and the group id, and no name or address), and a debug-log line. Works whether or not the Share to LinkedIn dialog is offered to that person.

user_id.description: WordPress user id of the person whose saved LinkedIn groups to use. 404 user_not_found when no such user. Digits only; the list read or written is that person's and nobody else's.

id.description: The numeric LinkedIn group id to remove, as list returns it (digits only, no leading zero). A JSON string only.

operations.returns: data: {user_id, groups[], count, max}; groups is the person's whole list after the call, in saved order, each {id, name, url}: id is LinkedIn's numeric group id as a string, name the saved name, url the page the group opens at (https://www.linkedin.com/groups/{id}/); count is the number saved and max the most one person may save (20)

operations.summary: Read the site time zone (WordPress Settings, General). It decides when a callback follow-up is due today and the times the portal shows. city is true for a region zone such as America/Detroit; note recommends one otherwise.

Set the site time zone the way the General settings screen stores a city zone (timezone_string set, gmt_offset emptied). One identifier from PHP's timezone_identifiers_list(): a city zone such as America/Detroit is recommended (daylight saving follows it); UTC is accepted; a raw offset (UTC+5), a backward-compatible alias (US/Eastern) or anything else is 422 invalid_timezone and nothing changes. The offset is emptied only after the zone is read back (a save that did not stick is 500 write_failed and leaves both as they were). A changed zone re-arms the events pinned to a site-time hour (the 02:00 FlowMattic orphan sweep).

timezone_string.description: A time zone identifier, for example America/Detroit.
